text:
olivia: noticed a sudden p99 jump on hosted API around 09:12 UTC, from ~120ms to ~750ms. dashboard shows queue depth creeping on frontend pools. anyone oncall can start triage?

sre-bot: alert: hosted.api.p99 > 600ms (09:12:18). affected clusters: hosted-us-east-1-a, hosted-us-east-1-b. topology: gpu-serving-pool-4. rate of requests +58% in last 2m.

mike: looking. initial hunch: kernel selector change we rolled yesterday could be mispicking for short-seq fast paths and causing batch fragmentation. can someone dump selector decisions?

raj: grabbing traces and sproc flame. quick summary from perf agent: increased ``coalesce_wait_ms`` and ``aux_kernel_fallback`` spikes. sample stack counts show more time in `kv_prefetch` / `batch_coalesce` than usual.

jen: KV cache metrics: eviction rate x6, hot shard 172.16.9.34 shows TTL churn. tenant-42 has huge burst of small requests (seq_len 8) — looks like a noisy customer pattern. cache miss rate up 42%.

luis: that noisy tenant + selector preferring larger-kernel batches for medium seqs could be creating a mismatch: short requests waiting for coalescing into larger batches, then aux kernel fallback when memory not enough. results in long tail.

mike: exactly. selector A/B was nudged towards throughput yesterday (`kselector.v2` weight increased). can we roll that canary back to baseline for affected pools?

olivia: on it. applying temporary rate cap to tenant-42 (50r/s) while we revert selector canary. will also pin hosted-us-east-1-a to kernel-v1 for short sequences.

raj: attaching quick profiler snippet:

```
09:12:05 request=abc123 tenant=tenant-42 seq_len=8 chosen_kernel=kopt_large coalesce_wait_ms=38 kv_prefetch_ms=12 aux_fallback=true total_ms=732
09:12:07 request=def456 tenant=tenant-42 seq_len=6 chosen_kernel=kopt_large coalesce_wait_ms=44 kv_prefetch_ms=15 aux_fallback=true total_ms=814
```

jen: evictions dropping after rate cap applied. eviction_rate host=172.16.9.34 before=720/s after=130/s. p95 falling but p99 still noisy.

mike: starting revert: `kselector.set_weight --pool hosted-us-east-1-a --version kselector.v1` — rolling this out as fast rollback.

deploy-bot: rollout started for kselector revert to kselector.v1 on hosted-us-east-1-a (change-id: revert-175888)

luis: also recommend increasing short-seq batching patience threshold from 10ms -> 25ms temporarily so tiny requests can coalesce without triggering large-kernel picks.

mike: applying patience tweak to canary pool now: `runtime-config set batching.short_seq_patience_ms 25 --pool hosted-us-east-1-a`

raj: traces show immediate improvement on new decisions, aux_fallback occurrences down 80% in canary logs.

deploy-bot: rollout succeeded (change-id: revert-175888) at 09:13:42. 95% of nodes in pool now on kselector.v1.

olivia: monitoring: p95 back to ~140ms, p99 down to ~240ms and trending. still watching for remaining tails.

jen: follow-up items: 1) add per-tenant burst protection for small-seq patterns; 2) add a safety-guard in kselector that avoids choosing large kernel if coalesce_wait > X ms; 3) increase KV cache diagnostic retention for 30m after spikes.

mike: agree. I'll open a short RFC for selector safety-guards and a one-off tuning playbook for host-edge noisy tenants.

olivia: thanks everyone — keeping this thread open for a bit while SLA graphs stabilize. :thumbsup:

luis: +1, recommend postmortem if we see recurrence within 72h.

olivia: will file incident if it reappears. closing updates in 30m.
